subject: science
passage: A tumbleweed starts its life as an ordinary rooted plant. In late summer, after it has flowered, the whole plant dries out and its stem becomes brittle at the base. A strong wind then snaps the dead plant free, and it begins to roll across the open ground. ______ it scatters its seeds, dropping a few at a time over a distance that can stretch for kilometers.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The text describes what happens to a tumbleweed in order: it dries, snaps free, and rolls across the ground. The last sentence describes what happens while it rolls: it drops seeds. A transition that connects this action to the rolling journey is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Dropping seeds is not an example of the plant rolling; it is what the plant does as it rolls.
explanation.B: Correct. "Along the way" shows that the seeds are scattered during the plant's rolling journey across the ground.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "In contrast" signals a difference, but scattering seeds is part of the rolling described just before, not an opposing idea.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Even so" signals something true despite the previous point, but nothing in the text works against the scattering of seeds.
